turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. I'll just do your obs before the doctor calls you. Blood pressure is 122 over 76, pulse is 78, and you're 81 kilograms on the scale.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Eish, 81. I was round about 68 when I finished varsity. The robot outside was chaos, hey, we sat there for ages.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hi, I'm Doctor Maseko. Sorry about the wait. What can I do for you today?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): It's my skin, mostly. The acne on my face just won't quit, and my periods are all over the show.
[SEG0005] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'm her mother. She's been stressing about the photos. Her cousin's wedding is in Durban and she keeps plastering on makeup.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, Mom, the wedding isn't why we're here. It's the spots and the periods that are actually bothering me. We nearly missed the turnoff as well, the sign is tiny.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): Alright. The periods. How long have they been irregular?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, about two years now. I'll skip a month, sometimes two. The last one was, I think, six weeks ago? Ja, more or less.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the acne, did that start around the same time?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh the lady at the salon was on about a charcoal mask, shame. She wanted four hundred rand a session. I told her no ways, I'm not made of money.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ja, the salon can wait. When did the acne itself start?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Sorry, sorry. Same sort of time, about two years. It's the chin and the jaw, and a bit on the cheeks. It gets worse just before a period, when I actually get one.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any hair where you wouldn't expect it, on the face or the chest?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, a bit of hair on the chin and the sideburns. I pluck it in the car before work. I work at the clothing shop in the mall, and the lights in there show everything.
[SEG0015] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She's put on weight as well. She still stays with me, so I see it.

[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Mom, please. I have put on weight, ja, maybe ten kilos over those two years. I'm not sitting eating koeksisters every day. I even tried the gym for a month and then the shift times got silly.

[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm thinking out loud, so stop me. Err, spots, cycles all over the place, a little facial hair, weight up. That cluster makes me wonder about polycystic ovaries, but it might also just be the weight and the cycles nudging each other. I don't want to put a label on you until we've looked properly.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever with all of this?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No fever.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): What about a cough, or being short of breath?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No, my chest is fine. Nothing like that.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): And headaches?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, not really. Not proper headaches. Sometimes after a long shift my head feels a bit tight, but I wouldn't call it a headache. I don't know, it's vague.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Okay, we'll leave that one. Are you using any medicines at the moment?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): I put benzoyl peroxide gel on at night, the 5 percent, just on the spots. And if the period cramps are bad I take ibuprofen, 400 milligrams, maybe two days in the month.
[SEG0026] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Don't forget the antibiotic. The GP gave her doxycycline last year and she stopped it.

[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, the doxicycline. It was 100 milligrams once a day. I did about three months and it made my stomach horrible, so I stopped. That was last year. The GP's rooms didn't even have aircon, I remember that more than the tablets.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines, or anything else?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing I know of.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any diabetes in the family? With the weight and the cycles I always ask.
[SEG0031] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ja, I've got type 2 diabetes. Diagnosed about eight years back. Her father doesn't have it.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke? And alcohol?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't smoke. I'll have a cider at a braai, not every weekend, one or two. My uncle braais every second Saturday and he always offers, hey.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right. I was going to start you on a combined pill today, Yasmin, one tablet a day. It often settles the skin and the cycle.
[SEG0035] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She gets those bad headaches with the flashing lights. Migraines. I told the other GP, it happens.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Mom, that's like twice a year, with the zigzags in my eyes. I didn't think it was a big deal.

[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ah, that changes it. If there's migraine with the visual aura, I'm not happy putting you on a combined pill today. Scratch the Yasmin. We'll park the pill completely, and rather do bloods and a pelvic scan before we pick any treatment.
[SEG0038] person_1 (NURSE): I can book the bloods at the lab downstairs, and radiology has a pelvic scan slot on Thursday if you want it.

[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ja, let's do that. Hormone bloods, a fasting glucose because of your mom's diabetes, and the pelvic ultrasound on Thursday. Come back in three weeks and we'll go through the results. Keep using the ibuprofen the way you have been if the cramps bite, and don't start any contraceptive pill in the meantime.

spec.situation: Young woman with acne and irregular periods for two years, some facial hair, weight gain; mother had diabetes; bloods and pelvic scan planned; contraceptive pill discussed, not started.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

features: doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.

omissions.text: Last menstrual period was about six weeks ago.
Irregular periods described as skipping a month and sometimes two months; recorded frequency omits the explicit possibility of skipping two months and the last period timing.
Weight gain was quantified as about 10 kg over the past two years.
Headaches were specifically asked about and the patient said not really/no proper headaches, only a vague tight head after long shifts; this uncertainty/near-negative response is not recorded.
Stopped doxycycline because it made her stomach feel horrible (GI side effect).
Doctor initially planned to start Yasmin, one tablet daily, for acne/cycle control.
Combined oral contraceptive plan was then cancelled after migraine with visual aura was disclosed; doctor said 'scratch the Yasmin' and to avoid combined pill because of aura.
